skill_traces.query:
Joanna: Nate, after finishing my screenplay I got a rejection letter from a major company. It really bummed me out.
Nate: Sorry to hear that, Joanna. Rejection stinks, but it doesn't mean you're not talented. Don't give up on your dreams!
Joanna: Thanks, Nate. It can feel like a step back sometimes. But I appreciate your kind words and encouragement.
Nate: Sure, just make sure you keep going and believing in yourself. Did something happen with the company?
Joanna: They just sent me a generic rejection letter without much feedback. It's disheartening not knowing why it didn't work out.
Nate: Ugh, that's so frustrating. But don't get discouraged, just keep going.
Joanna: Yeah, you're right. I won't let this bring me down. Thanks for your support. What have you been up to lately?
Nate: I've been doing great - I just won another regional video game tournament last week! It was so cool, plus I met some new people. Connecting with fellow gamers is always awesome.
Joanna: Way to go, Nate! Congratulations on your victory in the tournament! It must feel great to be recognized for your gaming skills.
Nate: Thanks, Joanna! Winning was a huge confidence boost and shows my hard work paid off. I'm really happy with my progress.
Joanna: I am as well! It's great to hear from you about your tournaments throughout the years!
Nate: Thanks! I has been a while since my first tournament hasn't it? I appreciate your support!
Joanna: Anytime Nate! I'm here for you every step of the way.
Nate: I talked to some of the guys at the tournament afterwards, and they said they wanted to hang out later!
Joanna: Sounds like fun! It's good to have friends that share your interests!
Nate: For sure! They asked for some tips in how to improve their game, so I said I could help.
Joanna: Good on you for helping strangers out! Stepping outside your comfort zone is always great.
Nate: Thanks, I just like helping people. Do you have any plans for the weekend?
Joanna: Yep, I'm hiking with some buddies this weekend. We're checking out a new trail with a rad waterfall. Can't wait! Do you have any fun plans?
Nate: Sounds great! Have fun with that. I'm organizing a gaming party two weekends later - it'll be hectic but fun!
Joanna: Oh? Are you going to invite your tournament friends?
Nate: Definitely! And some old friends and teamates from other tournaments.
Joanna: Sounds like fun, Nate! I wish you the best on your party. Have a blast!
Nate: Thanks Joanna! I'm sure it'll be a blast. I'm even getting everyone custom controller decorations just for coming!
Joanna: Wow, I bet they'll love that! What a sweet idea.
Nate: I know right? Have a great hike. Take lots of pics! See ya later!
Joanna: Thanks Nate! See you later!

nearby_not_selected.name: Capture likely deceased from euphemistic absence language
nearby_not_selected.description: During extraction, when a speaker describes someone with euphemistic absence language (e.g., 'will never be able to...', 'I miss him/her here') that strongly implies death, use this guidance.
content: When a statement euphemistically implies a person has died without explicitly saying so, also extract the implied state that the person is likely deceased, in addition to the literal statement.
Record the inference with an appropriate hedge (e.g., 'likely deceased') because the speaker did not state it directly; do not assert cause, date, or circumstances of death.
Stop after capturing the likely-deceased state and the literal content; do not extrapolate further details about the person or the relationship.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Photo-Sharing Events
nearby_not_selected.description: When a message presents an object or result with visual language like 'Here are...' or explicitly mentions sharing a photo, during extraction.
content: When a message uses presentation phrasing such as 'Here are...', 'Check out...', 'This is a photo of...', or 'Attached is...' to introduce something, record that the speaker shared a photo of that item, even if the word 'photo' does not appear.

If the speaker explicitly mentions sharing, sending, or showing a picture/photo/image, create an event memory that records the sharing action and the described content (e.g., subject or creator of the picture).
Preserve the literal object named in the message (e.g., picture) — do not replace it with an inferred object such as a bookshelf, item, or possession.
Keep the sharing act within the same event memory as the other facts from that message; do not summarize away the visual sharing.
Only include facts explicitly stated; do not convert a shared picture into an ownership claim unless ownership is directly stated.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Absolute Start Dates from Durations
nearby_not_selected.description: When a message states a relationship, tenure, or state has lasted for a duration (e.g., 'for three years'), extract the absolute start date using the message timestamp.
content: During extraction, if a message contains a duration phrase like 'for N years/months' describing an ongoing relationship, tenure, or state, resolve the reference timestamp (message/session time) minus the duration to an absolute date (year or full date) and include that absolute start in the memory content and/or world_start.
Do not store only the relative duration; the absolute date is needed for future temporal queries.
If the exact month/day is unknown, record at least the start year, phrasing it as 'started in YYYY' or 'since YYYY'.
